per_shot.note: Warm, lived-in hall with good practicals; the Gallery doorway is only a dark slot with a tiny sign, and the lower 40% of the frame is a flat, matte dark floor with nothing on it except the suit's beam.

The structure is right (plinths, glass cases, placards, spotlights, coloured pools on the floor), but the stones themselves are dim and greyed, so they read as pale glass shapes rather than lit treasures.

The four colour-coded tanks wash the walls and floor well and the creatures read as silhouettes, but the creatures are flat-lit, with no inner glow of their own; the ceiling and back wall fall to near-black.

top_issues.issue: Gallery stones do not glow; they look like tinted glass, not museum pieces
top_issues.why: The direction asks for stones lit like showpieces, with emissives blooming into the dark. Here the case halos are brighter than the gems inside them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make each stone the brightest thing in its case. Give it an emissive core in its own hue with a soft bloom, and keep the facets visible.

top_issues.issue: Large dead floor in the lower frame
top_issues.why: The bottom third is a flat dark slab, so light does not land enough to make the room feel rich.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the pools from the lamps, cases and portholes reach further across the floor plating, or add a subtle sheen so the floor carries the light sources.

top_issues.issue: Vivarium creatures are lit from outside rather than glowing
top_issues.why: The brief says the creatures are remembered as light and the tanks glow with living light. The tank tint is doing all the work.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add emissive accents on each creature (eye, core, fin edges) in its world hue so the creature becomes the light source.

top_issues.why: The brief rules out a black slab for a ceiling, and the hall's warm ceiling structure is lost in the wings.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Carry some of the coloured spill up onto the ceiling ribs and spotlight housings so the room keeps its shape.

protect: The plinth, glass case, placard and overhead spotlight layout in the Gallery reads as a museum
The coloured floor pools under each case and tank, one hue per exhibit
The Vivarium's colour-coded tank rims and the light they wash onto the walls
The warm hall lighting with the arc lamp, sconces and porthole dusk
The suit stays the brightest, cleanest read in every frame

per_shot.note: Same room as A, but a glossy floor now carries warm reflections of every light source, which fills the old dead floor. The streaks read a little wet, a hard red-and-black band cuts across the bottom edge, and the Gallery doorway is still an under-sold dark slot.

The stones now glow and bloom like museum pieces, and the floor carries a reflection in each stone's hue, so this is clearly a showpiece. Ruby and diamond cores blow out close to white and lose some of their hue.
The creatures gain inner glow hot spots and the floor reflects each tank's colour. Better than A, but the glow is spot-like rather than whole-body, and the ceiling and back wall are still near-black.

top_issues.issue: Bloom clips gem cores to white
top_issues.why: Ruby, voidopal and diamond lose their identifying hue at the centre, which weakens the one-hue-per-exhibit read.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Cap the emissive intensity or tone-map the gem cores so each one stays saturated in its own colour, with bloom only at the edge.

top_issues.issue: Floor reflections read as wet and streaky, and a hard band cuts the bottom edge
top_issues.why: Long vertical streaks read as a puddle rather than hab plating, and the red-and-black strip at the bottom edge looks like a seam in the render.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Roughen the floor so the reflections become soft pools, and end or soften the front floor edge so no hard stripe crosses the frame.

top_issues.why: Small white hot spots sit on otherwise flat bodies, so the creatures do not yet read as made of light.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Spread the emissive along each silhouette (rims, fins, spine) in the tank's hue, not one white point.

top_issues.issue: Wing ceilings and back walls still go black
top_issues.why: The room loses its structure above the exhibits, against the no-black-slab direction.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the exhibit light catch the ceiling ribs and the spotlight housings.

top_issues.issue: The Gallery entrance does not tease the wing
top_issues.why: From the hall the wing is a dark doorway with a tiny placard; the showpiece is invisible until you enter.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let a little coloured case light spill through the doorway onto the hall floor.

protect: Gems as self-lit, blooming showpieces inside glass cases
Coloured floor light under each exhibit, in that exhibit's hue
The museum layout: plinths, cases, placards and overhead spots
The Vivarium tank colours and creature silhouettes
The warm hall practicals, and the suit staying legible against the brighter floor

why: B makes the exhibits glow and the light land on the floor, which is what turns the wings into showpieces; A has the same layout but dim, greyed gems and a dead floor. B's main debts are hue clipping on the gem cores, wet-looking streaks and the hard bottom band.
